tasks.short: Check the curriculum and student plans, plan lessons with colleagues, fill in the shared lesson schedule, book rooms and support staff, and share the plan with assistants.

steps.what: Special education teacher checks the curriculum plan and student plans before the planning meeting
Special education teacher confers with other staff members to plan and schedule lessons
Special education teacher fills in the shared lesson schedule in a spreadsheet
Special education teacher e-mails to book rooms and support staff for the lessons
Special education teacher e-mails the plan to the teaching assistants

tasks.design: A shared planner in the learning platform ({LMS}) shows the curriculum goals and the students' plan goals, counts goal coverage as lessons are placed in weeks, and books rooms and support staff from the same screen. Assistants see the plan as soon as it is saved. Planning lessons with colleagues stays in the meeting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans were kept in spreadsheets and rooms and staff booked by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning platforms offer shared planners with room booking.
tasks.still_hard: Timetable changes and absent colleagues upset plans.
tasks.human_edge: Agreeing which colleague can best take the hardest group.

reach.learn: Whether assistants prepare better when plans are visible earlier.

evidence.claim: Learning platforms offer shared lesson planners with goal coverage and room booking.
Staff councils must consent to tools that can monitor staff.

assumptions: Boundary: from approved curricula to assistants informed; teaching is outside.
Input contract: curricula approved by the school; rooms in the school's booking system; fallback is spreadsheets and e-mail.
The planning meeting does not change.
Colleagues' time is outside the teacher's savings.
research_questions: Are goals covered more evenly across the year?

already_counted.description: Special education teacher reads the goals view.

incremental.description: Special education teacher keeps the planner current after changes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare a student summary, send it to the professionals, discuss the student's needs and progress in the case meeting, record conclusions and update the student plan.

steps.what: Special education teacher prepares a student summary for the case meeting
Special education teacher e-mails the summary to the professionals
Special education teacher meets with other professionals to discuss individual students' needs and progress
Special education teacher writes the meeting's conclusions
Special education teacher updates the student plan with the conclusions

tasks.design: A summary template in the student records system ({OTHER}) fills marks, incidents and plan goals for the last period, and the teacher adds the question for the meeting. Once the teacher has checked it, and parents have consented to sharing, it goes to the professionals by secure mail. Conclusions are entered per plan goal so the plan updates from the same form. The meeting itself stays the same.
tasks.previous_blocker: Summaries were written from scratch and conclusions copied into the plan by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Records systems fill summary templates and link notes to plan goals.
tasks.still_hard: Professionals from outside often use their own forms.
tasks.human_edge: Speaking up for what the student said they need.

reach.learn: Whether summaries sent ahead shorten meetings.

evidence.claim: Student records systems fill summary templates and link notes to plan goals.
Sharing a student's data with professionals outside the school needs the parents' consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from student records to the updated plan; actions by outside professionals are outside.
Input contract: records in the student system; consent recorded by the school; fallback is writing by hand.
Professionals' time is outside the teacher's savings.
research_questions: Do plans reflect meeting conclusions sooner?

already_counted.description: Special education teacher checks the filled summary.

incremental.description: Special education teacher checks consent before sharing.

approvals.approved_version: The summary as checked by the teacher in s1; changes need a new check before sending.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is the meeting.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Judge whether a student is ready for mainstream classes, discuss the placement with the receiving school, parents and student, compile and send the transfer file and follow up how the student settles.

steps.what: Special education teacher judges whether a student is ready for mainstream classes
Special education teacher coordinates placement of students into mainstream classes with the school, parents and student
Special education teacher compiles the transfer file with plan, reports and marks
Special education teacher posts the transfer file to the receiving school
Special education teacher follows up how the student settles in the new class

tasks.design: The student records system ({OTHER}) exports a transfer file with the plan, reports and marks in the standard format schools exchange; the teacher checks what is included, and once checked it goes to the receiving school through the secure exchange. Judging readiness, agreeing the placement and following up stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Transfer files were put together by hand and posted.
tasks.enabler_now: Dutch schools exchange student files digitally between record systems.
tasks.still_hard: The right moment for a move depends on the student, not the file.
tasks.human_edge: Preparing a student for the noise and size of a mainstream class.

reach.learn: Whether complete files help the first weeks.

evidence.claim: Dutch school record systems exchange student files digitally between schools.
Parents must be informed about which student data go to the receiving school.

assumptions: Boundary: from student progress to settling checked; the receiving school's intake is outside.
Input contract: plan and reports in the records system; fallback is paper.
Judging, agreeing and following up do not change.
The receiving school's time is outside the teacher's savings.
research_questions: Do transferred students settle better with complete files?

already_counted.description: Special education teacher checks what the file includes.

incremental.description: Special education teacher explains the file to parents.

approvals.approved_version: The transfer file as checked by the teacher in s3; changes need a new check before sending.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is judgement and conversation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select the curriculum goals for the students' exit profile, draft the course outline with objectives per term, check goal coverage, get the department head's approval, publish the outline and adapt it during the year.

steps.what: Special education teacher selects curriculum goals that fit the students' exit profile
Special education teacher prepares objectives and outlines for courses of study per term

loop.input: The selected goal codes, the school calendar and last year's outline; no student data.
loop.output: A draft outline with objectives per term, each tagged with goal codes.
loop.check: Code checks every selected goal appears at least once and all dates fall in the calendar; the teacher edits every term.
loop.stop: Approved by the teacher, or after two redrafts the teacher writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Objectives must be phrased for this group; a fixed outline does not fit.

steps.what: Special education teacher checks goal coverage against the school's requirements
Department head approves the course outline
Special education teacher e-mails the outline to students and parents
Special education teacher adapts the outline when goals change during the year

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts the course outline with objectives per term from the selected goal codes, the calendar and last year's outline, and the teacher edits every term. Code checks goal coverage against the school's list. Once the department head has approved it, the learning platform ({LMS}) publishes the outline to students and parents. Selecting goals and adapting the outline stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Outlines were rewritten each year and coverage counted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft outlines from goal codes, and platforms publish them.
tasks.still_hard: In a randomised trial, teachers used a lesson assistant for few lessons and use declined.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing goals that prepare a student for a real job placement.
tasks.altitude: The teacher edits a drafted outline instead of rewriting it.

reach.learn: Whether coverage checks speed up approval.

evidence.claim: In a randomised trial with 464 primary teachers, Aila cut weekly preparation from 3.3 to 2.5 hours with quality no worse, but covered 7% of lessons and use declined over ten weeks.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes or sets a pupil's level is high-risk; drafting outlines does neither.

assumptions: Boundary: from curriculum guidelines to the revised outline; teaching is outside.
Input contract: goal codes from the national curriculum; calendar from the school office; fallback is writing by hand.
Selecting goals and adapting do not change.
The department head's time is outside the teacher's savings.
research_questions: How much of the drafted outline survives editing?

already_counted.description: Special education teacher edits the drafted outline.
Special education teacher reviews the coverage check.

incremental.description: Special education teacher keeps the goal list current.

approvals.approved_version: The outline as approved by the department head in s4; changes need a new approval before publishing.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Teachers may use the drafting step for only part of their outlines.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The special education teacher keeps planning with colleagues, case meetings, placement judgement and goal choices; spreadsheets, summaries and outlines written from scratch shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher whose planning paperwork is ready before the meeting starts.
